origin.fact: It is an aquarium colour form of the southern platy, Xiphophorus maculatus. The wild species lives from Mexico to northern Belize.

No single developer is credited. Glaser, a German importer, says the colours in Mickey Mouse platies have been known in platies for decades. Breeders combine them into new pure-bred colour forms rather than creating new breeds.

The Mickey Mouse tail mark, which breeders call 'moon complete', was uncommon in early Bleeding Heart platies. Bleeding Heart platies were developed by geneticist Myron Gordon in the 1940s and today almost always carry this tail mark.

looks.fact: The defining mark is a large dark spot at the base of the tail with two smaller round spots above it, like Mickey Mouse's head and ears.
The trade also calls this mark the 'moon complete' pattern.
Body colour varies: pale gold, yellow, orange, red or bluish. Fins may be red, black-edged or pale yellow. High-fin and long-fin forms exist.
A clear, well-formed three-spot mark is the main feature buyers look for. Fish carrying two copies of the gene have a darker, larger spot group, sold as 'large spot' or 'extreme' Mickey.
Females are larger and duller than males. Males have a gonopodium.

lines.fact: Colour forms sold include White, Blue, Red, Marigold, Marlboro, Hi-fin and Emerald Mickey Mouse platies.
Tiger Mickey Mouse platy: orange, white, red and silver with tiger-like bars.
White Red Tail Mickey Mouse: snow-white body, clear fins and sky-blue eyes, with a red patch on the back. In dominant males the red patch spreads down the belly toward the tail.
Bleeding Heart Mickey Mouse: a Bleeding Heart platy (white body, red throat patch, blue eyes) that also has the Mickey Mouse tail mark.
Assorted or mixed Mickey Mouse platies are sold as a mix of colours.

keeping.fact: Use at least a 10-gallon (about 38 L) tank. A standard tank of that size is about 50 cm long. Keep a group of 6–8 fish.
A thickly planted tank with hardy plants such as Java fern and Java moss suits them.
Use a sponge filter or a hang-on-back filter with adjustable flow, and avoid strong currents. Hard, alkaline water close to typical tap water is fine.
They are omnivores. Feed flakes and pellets, plus frozen or freeze-dried food and vegetables such as cooked peas, spinach or zucchini. Feed twice a day, only what they eat in a few minutes.
Dark gravel or sand shows their colours well. They may nibble live plants.

They are peaceful. Good tankmates include other platies, guppies, mollies, swordtails, catfish, gouramis, tetras and danios. Avoid large or semi-aggressive fish. Shrimp and snails make good clean-up crews.

breeding.fact: They are livebearers that breed easily. They can breed from about 4 months old. Pregnancy lasts about 30 days, and each brood has 40–60 fry.
Females can store sperm and give birth several times without mating again.
Adults eat fry. Use dense plants or a separate nursery tank. Feed fry several times a day and change their water daily.

One Singapore guide says the mark comes from a single, incompletely dominant tail-pattern gene. Mickey × Mickey gives about 25% plain, 50% normal Mickey and 25% double-dose fry. Mickey × plain gives about 50% Mickey. Only double-dose × double-dose pairs breed true. The guide itself calls these ratios speculative.
A group in a home tank will breed without help. Offspring are fertile because the fish is a single species.

health.fact: Generally hardy, but can catch common diseases such as velvet, white spot (ich), bacterial infections and skin flukes. Quarantine new fish and plants.
Feeding only protein-rich food is discouraged. A plant-rich, varied diet is advised.
Lifespan is about 5 years with good care.

buying.fact: Easy to find in fish shops and online. They are cheap, and buying several often lowers the price per fish.
Check the tail mark. A single-copy fish shows a clean three-spot mark, while a double-dose fish has a darker, larger spot group.
Shops usually sell them at 2–3 cm (3/4–1 1/4 in). Adults reach about 5 cm (2 in).
To sex them for breeding, look for the male's gonopodium and pointed anal fin. Females are larger.

controversy.fact: Non-native platy populations live in the wild in several US states, including Florida, Texas and California, most likely from aquarium releases. The source says this about the species, not about the Mickey Mouse form in particular.
